# How the Laughing Box Animation Is Made

This guide explains, step by step, how every Laughing Box episode (for example [Episode 6, "Grandpa's First Flight"](../episodes/06-grandpas-first-flight/)) is produced: the tools, the setup, what each script does, the techniques behind the movement, voices and sound, and how to make the next episode yourself.

**The short version:** there is no drawing program and no video editor. Every frame, voice, sound effect and note of music is **generated by Python code**. You describe the story in a text file, run four scripts, and FFmpeg joins the picture and sound into a 4K vertical video.

```
 idea ─▶ timeline.py ─▶ make_video.py ──▶ picture.mp4 ─┐
 (story)   (shots,       (draws every      (silent 4K)  │
            lines,        frame with Cairo)             ├─▶ ffmpeg ─▶ episode-4k.mp4
            SFX cues) ─▶ make_voice.py ─▶ voice_track ─┐│   (mix + loudness)
                          (Kokoro TTS)    .wav/.json   ││
                       ─▶ make_audio.py ──▶ soundtrack ─┘
                          (synth SFX + music + ducking)
                       ─▶ make_thumbnail.py ─▶ cover-1080x1920.png
```

---

## 1. Tools used

All tools are **free**. Everything runs offline on your own computer after the one-time downloads.

| Tool | What it does in Laughing Box | Cost / licence | Get it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Python 3.10+** | The language every script is written in | Free (PSF) | [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/) |
| **Cairo + pycairo** | 2D vector drawing library. Draws characters, sets, props, captions as shapes with thick outlines (the "cartoon" look) | Free (LGPL/MPL) | `pip install pycairo` |
| **NumPy** | Fast number arrays: audio samples, mixing, envelopes | Free (BSD) | `pip install numpy` |
| **SciPy** | Audio filters (low-pass, band-pass) for SFX, music and the "airplane speaker" pilot voice | Free (BSD) | `pip install scipy` |
| **Kokoro TTS** (`kokoro-onnx`) | Text-to-speech: turns each script line into a character voice, offline | Free, open weights (Apache-2.0), commercial use allowed | `pip install kokoro-onnx` + 2 model files (below) |
| **librosa** | Trims silence, pitch-shifts voices (Grandpa lower, Leo higher), resamples | Free (ISC) | `pip install librosa` |
| **soundfile** | Reads/writes audio files (used by Kokoro/librosa) | Free (BSD) | `pip install soundfile` |
| **FFmpeg** | Encodes frames into H.264 video, mixes in the soundtrack, sets loudness to −14 LUFS, makes the contact sheet | Free (LGPL/GPL) | [ffmpeg.org](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html) |
| **Git + GitHub** | Stores every script and video, history of every change | Free | [git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/) |
| **An AI coding agent** *(optional but recommended)* | Writes and edits the scripts for a new episode by following the repo's skill file | Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Hoplite | See [`../claude/README.md`](../claude/README.md) |
| **Any image viewer** | Checking stills, the contact sheet and the cover | Free | Built into your OS |

What is **not** used: no Photoshop, After Effects, CapCut, Premiere, stock music, sound libraries, downloaded fonts or AI image/video generators. That is why everything is 100 % original and owned by the channel, and why a character always looks exactly the same in every episode.

> Want a different look (painterly, AI-generated, hand-animated)? See [tools-and-workflow.md](tools-and-workflow.md) for the AI-first and 2D-animation toolchains. They can use the same story and shot-list structure.

## 2. One-time setup

### 2.1 Install Python, FFmpeg and Cairo

**Windows**

1. Install Python 3.10+ from python.org. Tick **"Add Python to PATH"**.
2. Install FFmpeg: `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg` (or download from ffmpeg.org and add its `bin` folder to PATH).
3. Cairo comes inside the `pycairo` wheel on Windows. Nothing extra is needed.

**macOS**

```bash
brew install python cairo pkg-config ffmpeg
```

**Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)**

```bash
sudo apt-get install -y python3 python3-venv python3-dev libcairo2-dev pkg-config ffmpeg
```

### 2.2 Get the project and the Python packages

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Bidyut27/video-reference-analysis.git
cd video-reference-analysis
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate          # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install pycairo numpy scipy kokoro-onnx soundfile librosa
```

### 2.3 Download the voice model (once, ~350 MB)

From the [kokoro-onnx model release](https://github.com/thewh1teagle/kokoro-onnx/releases/tag/model-files-v1.0) download:

- `kokoro-v1.0.onnx`
- `voices-v1.0.bin`

Put both in one folder, e.g. `~/kokoro/`. This folder is the `MODEL_DIR` in the commands below. Do **not** commit these files to Git; they are large.

### 2.4 Check it works

```bash
python -c "import cairo, numpy, scipy, librosa, kokoro_onnx; print('ok')"
ffmpeg -version
```

## 3. What is inside an episode folder

Every episode lives in `laughing-box/episodes/NN-slug/`. Episode 6 as the example:

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `timeline.py` | **The story.** Shot list with durations, sound-effect cues and every dialogue line. All other scripts read it, so picture, voice and sound stay in sync |
| `make_video.py` | **The picture.** One drawing function per shot; renders every frame and pipes them into FFmpeg |
| `make_voice.py` | **The voices.** Speaks each line with Kokoro, checks it fits its shot, writes `voice_track.wav` + `voice_track.json` (caption timing and mouth movement) |
| `make_audio.py` | **The sound.** Synthesises SFX and music, places them on the cues, ducks them under dialogue, writes `soundtrack.wav` |
| `make_thumbnail.py` | **The 9:16 cover** (1080×1920) |
| `ep1.py` | Loader that imports characters, sets, props, SFX and music from earlier episodes, so nothing is redrawn and the cast stays on-model |
| `voice_track.wav` / `.json` | Output of `make_voice.py` (kept so the video can be rebuilt without the voice model) |
| `grandpas-first-flight-4k.mp4` | **Final video** (2160×3840, 24 fps) |
| `cover-1080x1920.png` | **Final cover** |
| `contact-sheet.jpg` | One frame every 2 s for quick review |
| `README.md` | Story beats, posting copy for YouTube/Facebook/Instagram, rebuild commands |

Shared folders:

| Folder | What it gives every episode |
|---|---|
| `laughing-box/characters/` | Every character as a transparent PNG, cast poster, expression sheets |
| `laughing-box/brand-kit/` | Logo, profile picture, banners, watermark |
| `.agents/skills/laughing-box-episode/references/series-bible.md` | Character names, colours, outfits, voices, sets, episode log: the "rules" of the show |
| `laughing-box/production/blueprint.md` | Story structure, safe zones, audio rules |
| `laughing-box/production/templates.md` | QC checklist |

## 4. Step-by-step: making an episode

Approximate time for one episode with an AI coding agent doing the coding: **2–4 hours**, most of it reviewing. By hand: 1–3 days.

### Step 1: Pick the idea (10 min)

- One universal, relatable situation that is funny **with the sound off** (planes, smart speakers, self-checkouts, homework).
- Alternate "Grandpa/Grandma vs. *thing*" episodes with episodes for other characters, so the channel isn't one joke.
- Check the episode log in the series bible so you don't repeat a premise.

### Step 2: Write the story in `timeline.py` (30–60 min)

The structure every episode follows:

| Time | Beat | Episode 6 example |
|---|---|---|
| 0–3 s | **Hook**: absurd image, no slow intro | Grandpa pressing the call button, *bing bing bing bing* |
| 3–10 s | **Setup** | "Metal can't fly. It's science!" |
| 10–30 s | **3 escalations** | Seat belt too short → life vest inflates → takeoff panic |
| before ~35 s | **New character** arrives | Rosa the flight attendant, the pilot |
| ~40 s | **Twist 1** | He loves the sunset |
| ~48 s | **Twist 2** | They've landed already, and he's stuck in the vest |
| last 4 s | **Button** that loops back to the hook | Back to the call button |

Rules: something changes on screen at least every 2 s; 18–24 shots; 15–20 lines; lines short and simple (≤ 8 words where possible); total 55–75 s.

The file is plain data:

```python
SHOTS = [
    # (shot name, seconds, [(time inside shot, "sound effect"), ...])
    ("hook_button", 2.6, [(0.15, "bing"), (0.55, "bing"), (0.95, "bing"), (1.35, "bing")]),
    ("attendant_sigh", 2.4, [(0.1, "squeak")]),
    ("vest_poof", 2.8, [(0.0, "inflate"), (0.45, "impact"), (0.5, "pop")]),
    ...
]

LINES = [
    # (shot, seconds into the shot, speaker, line)
    ("attendant_sigh", 0.3, "rosa", "Yes, sir... again?"),
    ("cabin_wide", 0.3, "grandpa", "Metal can't fly. It's science!"),
    ...
]
```

Change a number here and the picture, voice and sound all move together.

### Step 3: Draw the shots in `make_video.py` (1–2 h)

Each shot is a Python function that draws one frame at time `t`:

```python
# Episode 6, the life vest inflating (shortened)
def sh_vest_poof(ctx, t, d, g):
    # t = seconds into this shot, d = shot length, g = global frame number
    k = eback(clamp(t / 0.45))          # 0→1 in 0.45 s with a cartoon overshoot
    laugh = t > 0.9
    cabin_row(ctx, t, [                 # the three plane seats with the family in them
        dict(P=GRANDPA, expr="shock", vest=k),            # vest inflates with k
        dict(P=GRANDMA, expr="shock", look=(-1, 0), dx=40 * k),   # pushed aside
        dict(P=LEO, expr="happy" if laugh else "shock", look=(-1, 0)),
    ], scene="runway")
    if 0.45 < t < 0.75:
        impact_star(ctx, 250, 1250, 260 * clamp((t - 0.45) / 0.15), seed=g)
    pop_text(ctx, "POOF!", 300, 620, 170, "#ff8c1a", t, 0.45, rot=-0.08)
```

All shots are listed in `SHOT_FUNCS`, which must match the shot names in `timeline.py`.

How the drawing works:

- **Canvas:** 1080×1920 coordinates, rendered at `SCALE=2`, so the output is native **2160×3840 (4K)** with no upscaling blur.
- **Characters are code, not images.** Grandpa, Grandma, Leo, Rosa and the others are built from ellipses, rounded rectangles and curves, filled with flat colours and given a thick dark outline (`OL = 7`). Because each one is a function like `person(ctx, x, y, scale, GRANDPA, pose, expr="shock")`, they are **always on-model**.
- **Expressions:** `face()` supports `neutral`, `happy`, `shock`, `furious`, `smug`, `nervous`, `suspicious`, `cry`, `wink`, `yawn` and `victory`: eyebrows, eyes, pupils (`look=`) and mouth change shape. See the expression sheets in `laughing-box/characters/`.
- **Reuse:** new episodes import earlier ones through `ep1.py` (`ep1.video()`, `ep1.ep2_video()` …), so the living room, armchair, phone, Leo and all the SFX are reused rather than redrawn. Only new things (Episode 6: airplane cabin, seats, call button, life vest, window views, plane exterior, Rosa) are drawn fresh.

Animation techniques used (all in episode 1's `make_video.py`):

| Technique | Helper | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Easing | `eio`, `eout`, `eback` | Smooth starts/stops; `eback` overshoots for a cartoon "pop" |
| Camera | `cam(ctx, z, fx, fy, rot, shake_amp)` | Push-ins, crash zooms, tilts |
| Screen shake | `shake(t, t0, amp)` | Hits and surprises |
| Flash | `flash(t, times)` | White flash on impacts |
| Walk cycle | `walk_pose(phase)` | Arm and leg swing |
| Blinks and idle | `blink=` in `person`/`face` | Characters feel alive in held shots |
| Vignette | `vignette(ctx, 0.25)` | Darkened edges that keep the eye centred |
| Stars, hearts, ✔/✖ | `star4`, `heart`, `check`, `xmark` | Comic overlays |
| Captions | `caption(ctx)` | Burned-in subtitles, colour per speaker, pop-in animation |

**Safe zones:** keep faces and text out of the top ~220 px, the bottom ~380 px and the right ~120 px (of the 1080×1920 canvas), where the platform's buttons and captions sit.

**Review before rendering:**

```bash
cd laughing-box/episodes/06-grandpas-first-flight
python make_video.py --stills /tmp/stills     # one PNG per shot, a few seconds
```

Open every still: faces on-model, action readable, nothing cut off, props big enough. Fix and repeat. This is much faster than rendering the whole video.

### Step 4: Generate the voices with `make_voice.py` (2 min)

```bash
python make_voice.py ~/kokoro voice_track.wav voice_track.json
```

For each line, it:

1. Speaks the text with the speaker's Kokoro voice and speed.
2. Trims silence, then pitch-shifts (Grandpa −1.5 semitones, Leo +2.5).
3. Applies character effects: the pilot goes through a 350–3400 Hz band-pass + light distortion so he sounds like a cabin speaker; the smart speaker/kiosk gets a robotic ring-mod.
4. Places it at its shot time and **checks it ends before the next line starts**. It must print `ALL LINES FIT`. If not, lengthen the shot or shorten the line.
5. Saves the loudness of every frame to `voice_track.json`. `make_video.py` reads this to **open the mouths in time with the words** (lip-sync) and to show captions exactly while each line plays.

Cast voices (Kokoro voice, speed, pitch shift):

| Character | Voice | Speed | Pitch |
|---|---|---|---|
| Grandpa Harold | `bm_george` (British male) | 0.95 | −1.5 |
| Grandma Margaret | `bf_emma` (British female) | 0.95 | 0 |
| Leo | `am_puck` (American male) | 1.1 | +2.5 |
| Rosa (flight attendant) | `af_sarah` (American female) | 1.05 | 0 |
| Pilot | `am_michael` + speaker filter | 0.95 | −1.0 |

The full list is in the series bible. Use the same voice for a character in every episode.

### Step 5: Build the soundtrack with `make_audio.py` (1 min)

```bash
VOICE_WAV=voice_track.wav python make_audio.py /tmp/soundtrack.wav
```

**Sound effects are synthesised from oscillators and noise**, with no samples:

- `whoosh` = filtered noise sweep; `pop` = short pitched blip; `impact` = low thump + noise burst
- `bing` = bell tone (sine partials with exponential decay); `taiko` = low drum hit
- `squeak`, `gulp`, `snore`, `sparkle`, `steam`, `engine`, `inflate`, `click`, `zoom`, `cork`, `sadtrombone`, `scratch` …

**Music** is generated too: `music()` builds the comedy theme from plucked/marimba notes, kick, snare and hi-hat; `pad()` makes a soft background chord.

The music plan used in every episode:

1. Quiet pad during the setup.
2. Comedy score enters on the first escalation.
3. **Silence drop** on the biggest gag (sudden quiet makes it land harder).
4. Light marimba for the twist.
5. Full score into the loop.

**Ducking:** while someone speaks, music drops ~60 % and SFX ~35 %, so every word is clear.

### Step 6: Render the 4K picture (~7 min on 4 CPU cores)

```bash
python make_video.py /tmp/picture.mp4            # 4K (default SCALE=2)
SCALE=1 python make_video.py /tmp/preview.mp4    # quick 1080p preview
```

The script draws all frames in parallel on every CPU core (`multiprocessing.Pool`) and streams the raw pixels straight into FFmpeg (`libx264`, `-crf 18`, `yuv420p`, `+faststart`). No temporary image files are written.

### Step 7: Mix picture + sound, normalise loudness

```bash
ffmpeg -i /tmp/picture.mp4 -i /tmp/soundtrack.wav \
  -filter:a "loudnorm=I=-14:TP=-2.5:LRA=11,alimiter=limit=0.84:level=false" \
  -c:v copy -c:a aac -b:a 192k -ar 48000 -shortest -movflags +faststart \
  grandpas-first-flight-4k.mp4
```

- `loudnorm I=-14` sets the volume to −14 LUFS, the level YouTube, Instagram and Facebook normalise to, so the video is never too quiet or too loud next to others.
- `alimiter` keeps peaks below clipping.
- `-c:v copy` keeps the 4K picture untouched (no second compression).

### Step 8: Check the result (QC)

```bash
ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=width,height,r_frame_rate,nb_frames -of csv=p=0 grandpas-first-flight-4k.mp4
ffmpeg -i grandpas-first-flight-4k.mp4 -af ebur128=peak=true -f null - 2>&1 | tail -12
ffmpeg -i grandpas-first-flight-4k.mp4 -vf "fps=1/2,scale=216:384,tile=6x5:padding=4" -frames:v 1 contact-sheet.jpg
```

Pass criteria (Episode 6 measured values in brackets):

- 2160×3840, 24 fps [✔ 2160×3840, 24 fps, 1,392 frames]
- 55–75 s [✔ 58 s]
- Integrated loudness ≈ −14 LUFS [✔ −14.0]; true peak ≤ −1 dBFS [✔ −2.0]
- `ALL LINES FIT` [✔]
- Contact sheet: every shot readable, no cut-off faces or text
- Watch it once on a phone with sound **on**, and once with sound **off** (captions must tell the story)

The full checklist is in [templates.md, section 5](templates.md).

### Step 9: Make the 9:16 cover (1 min)

```bash
python make_thumbnail.py .        # writes cover-1080x1920.png
```

- 1080×1920 (9:16) only. Laughing Box doesn't make 16:9 thumbnails.
- Headline of 2–4 huge words in the series style: white / **red** / white with thick outlines (`GRANDPA'S` / `FIRST` / `FLIGHT`).
- The main character's face large with a strong expression; the conflict readable without the text.
- Keep the title and face inside **y 240–1680**: Instagram's profile grid crops the cover to the centre 3:4.

### Step 10: Posting copy

Written into the episode `README.md` for each platform:

- **YouTube Shorts:** title + 2 emoji + `#shorts`, 2-line hook, "Welcome to Laughing Box: original cartoon comedy for everyone 🌍📦", subscribe line, 6–7 hashtags starting `#LaughingBox #CartoonComedy`. Audience: *No, it's not made for kids*. Category: Comedy.
- **Facebook Reel:** title, hook line, "📦 New Laughing Box episode!", a comment question ("Tag someone who…"), 5–6 hashtags.
- **Instagram Reel:** same as Facebook, plus `#Reels #Comedy #FunnyVideos`.
- Never use "kids", "children" or "nursery" in titles/tags. This risks a "Made for Kids" label (comments off, lower reach).

### Step 11: Upload

1. Upload the **4K MP4** to YouTube Shorts, Facebook Reels and Instagram Reels (each platform re-encodes; starting from 4K gives the sharpest result).
2. Upload `cover-1080x1920.png` as the cover/thumbnail where the platform allows it.
3. Paste the posting copy from the episode README.
4. Handle: **@Officiallaughingbox** on all platforms.

### Step 12: Save and log

- Add the episode to the log in the series bible and a row to `laughing-box/README.md`.
- New character? Add it to `CAST` in `laughing-box/characters/make_characters.py` and run it.
- Run `python laughing-box/claude/build_claude_files.py` so the AI-assistant copies stay up to date.
- Commit and push (no `__pycache__`, no temporary renders).

## 5. Making the next episode with an AI agent (the easy way)

The repo already contains everything an AI coding agent needs: [`AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md), the episode skill [`.agents/skills/laughing-box-episode/SKILL.md`](../../.agents/skills/laughing-box-episode/SKILL.md) and the series bible. Open the repo in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Antigravity or Hoplite and say:

```
Make Laughing Box episode 7. Give me 5 topic ideas first.
```

Pick one and say "go". The agent copies the newest episode folder, writes `timeline.py`, draws the new shots, generates voices and sound, renders 4K, makes the 9:16 cover and the posting copy, checks loudness and timing, and commits it. Your job is to **review the stills, the preview video and the cover**, and ask for changes ("make the vest bigger", "Grandpa's line is too long").

Only have ChatGPT/Gemini in a browser (no code execution)? Use [`chat-prompt.md`](../../.agents/skills/laughing-box-episode/references/chat-prompt.md) to get the script, shot list and posting copy, then run the scripts yourself.

## 6. Quick reference

### Final file specs

| Item | Spec |
|---|---|
| Video | 2160×3840 (9:16), 24 fps, H.264 High, CRF 18, yuv420p |
| Audio | AAC 192 kbps, 48 kHz stereo, −14 LUFS, peak ≤ −1 dBFS |
| Length | 55–75 s |
| Cover | 1080×1920 PNG, title + face inside y 240–1680 |
| Captions | Burned in, colour per character, inside the safe zone |

### All commands for one episode

```bash
cd laughing-box/episodes/NN-slug
python make_video.py --stills /tmp/stills                          # review stills
python make_voice.py ~/kokoro voice_track.wav voice_track.json     # must print ALL LINES FIT
VOICE_WAV=voice_track.wav python make_audio.py /tmp/soundtrack.wav
python make_video.py /tmp/picture.mp4                              # 4K render
ffmpeg -i /tmp/picture.mp4 -i /tmp/soundtrack.wav \
  -filter:a "loudnorm=I=-14:TP=-2.5:LRA=11,alimiter=limit=0.84:level=false" \
  -c:v copy -c:a aac -b:a 192k -ar 48000 -shortest -movflags +faststart NN-slug-4k.mp4
ffmpeg -i NN-slug-4k.mp4 -vf "fps=1/2,scale=216:384,tile=6x5:padding=4" -frames:v 1 contact-sheet.jpg
python make_thumbnail.py .
```

### Computer requirements

| | Minimum | Comfortable |
|---|---|---|
| CPU | 2 cores (4K render ~15 min) | 4–8 cores (~4–7 min) |
| RAM | 4 GB | 8 GB+ |
| Disk | 2 GB (tools + voice model) | + ~100 MB per episode |
| GPU | Not needed | Not needed |

## 7. Troubleshooting

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| `No module named 'cairo'` | Activate the virtual environment (`source .venv/bin/activate`), then `pip install pycairo`. On Linux/macOS install `libcairo2-dev`/`cairo` and `pkg-config` first |
| `ffmpeg: command not found` | Install FFmpeg and make sure it's on PATH (`ffmpeg -version`) |
| `SOME LINES DO NOT FIT` | Lengthen that shot in `timeline.py`, move the line earlier, or shorten the line. Then rerun voice, audio and video |
| Mouths don't move / no captions | `voice_track.json` is missing from the episode folder. Run `make_voice.py` first |
| Video too quiet/loud on the phone | You skipped the `loudnorm` mix step. Rerun step 7 |
| Render is slow | Use `SCALE=1` for previews; render 4K only for the final |
| Character looks different | Use the existing character function from `ep1.video()`. Never redraw a character |
| Text hidden behind app buttons | Move it inside the safe zone (section 4, step 3) |
| Cover cropped on Instagram grid | Keep title and face between y 240 and 1680 |

## 8. Originality and rights

- Every character, set, sound effect, piece of music and voice is generated by code in this repo, so Laughing Box owns it. Kokoro's Apache-2.0 licence allows commercial use of the generated speech.
- The reference videos in `reference-analysis/` are for studying **technique only**. Never upload, trace or copy them.
- Family-friendly: cartoon slapstick only, and the joke is the situation, never the person.
